accepted.s: Rashtriya Gram Swaraj Abhiyan (RGSA), which commenced in 2018-19, primarily aims at strengthening Panchayati Raj Institutions for achieving:
accepted.x: RGSA was introduced to strengthen Panchayati Raj Institutions and enable them to contribute to the achievement of Sustainable Development Goals.
accepted.tq: Identify the stated objective rather than a related development-sector objective.
accepted.sec: Capacity building - RGSA, NIRDPR and SIRDs, eGramSwaraj, AuditOnline  [APPSC]

accepted.s:
Consider the following statements regarding the Rashtriya Gram Swaraj Abhiyan (RGSA):
1. It seeks convergence with Mission Antyodaya.
2. It focuses on 117 aspirational districts.
3. It covers areas outside Part IX of the Constitution.
Which of the statements given above are correct?
accepted.x: RGSA promotes convergence with Mission Antyodaya, focuses on 117 aspirational districts and also covers areas outside Part IX.
accepted.tq: Test the scope and convergence features together; the inclusive statement about non-Part IX areas is important.
accepted.sec: Capacity building - RGSA, NIRDPR and SIRDs, eGramSwaraj, AuditOnline  [APPSC]

accepted.s: The funding pattern under RGSA is correctly represented by which one of the following?
o: Centre:State is 40:60, with 90:10 for Union Territories
Centre:State is 75:25, with no separate pattern for Union Territories
Centre:State is 60:40, 90:10 for North-Eastern and hilly States, and 100% Central funding for Union Territories
accepted.x: The normal Centre-State ratio is 60:40; it is 90:10 for North-Eastern and hilly States, while Union Territories receive 100% Central funding.
accepted.tq: Separate the normal ratio from the special ratios for difficult terrain and Union Territories.
accepted.sec: Capacity building - RGSA, NIRDPR and SIRDs, eGramSwaraj, AuditOnline  [APPSC]

accepted.s: The revamped RGSA is co-terminus with which period?
o: The Fifteenth Finance Commission period, from 1 April 2021 to 31 March 2026
The Fourteenth Finance Commission period, from 2015 to 2020
The Sixteenth Finance Commission period, from 1 April 2022 to 31 March 2027
The Fifteenth Finance Commission period, from 1 April 2022 to 31 March 2026
accepted.x: The revamped RGSA runs from 1 April 2022 to 31 March 2026 and matches the period of the Fifteenth Finance Commission. The 1 April 2021 starting date is incorrect.
accepted.tq: Discriminate between the close starting dates 1 April 2021 and 1 April 2022.
accepted.sec: Capacity building - RGSA, NIRDPR and SIRDs, eGramSwaraj, AuditOnline  [APPSC]

accepted.s: Which programme was merged into the Rashtriya Gram Swaraj Abhiyan?
accepted.x: The Backward Regions Grant Fund was merged into RGSA.
accepted.tq: Use the programme-merger relationship to distinguish RGSA from associated initiatives.
accepted.sec: Capacity building - RGSA, NIRDPR and SIRDs, eGramSwaraj, AuditOnline  [APPSC]

accepted.s: During 2025-26, the amount released under RGSA and the number of participants trained were, respectively:
accepted.x: The figures given for 2025-26 are ₹394.84 crore released and 8,67,915 participants trained. More than 35 lakh persons were reported as trained in FY25, which is a separate figure.
accepted.tq: Match the precise amount with the precise training count rather than the broader annual figure.
accepted.sec: Capacity building - RGSA, NIRDPR and SIRDs, eGramSwaraj, AuditOnline  [APPSC]

accepted.s: Which of the following correctly identifies the institutions associated with Panchayat training at the national and State levels?
o: NIRDPR at the national level and SIRDs in the States
SIRDs at the national level and NIRDPR in the States
NITI Aayog at the national level and DPCs in the States
Survey of India at the national level and MPCs in the States
accepted.x: The National Institute of Rural Development and Panchayati Raj (NIRDPR), Hyderabad, functions at the national level, while State Institutes of Rural Development function in the States.
accepted.tq: Match the institution with its administrative level.
accepted.sec: Capacity building - RGSA, NIRDPR and SIRDs, eGramSwaraj, AuditOnline  [APPSC]

accepted.s: Which one of the following correctly describes eGramSwaraj?
o: It provides only online auditing of Panchayat accounts.
It executes works recommended under MPLADS.
It combines Panchayat planning, accounting and reporting.
It prepares property records for rural homes.
accepted.x: eGramSwaraj integrates Panchayat planning, accounting and reporting. Online auditing is the specific function of AuditOnline, while property records are associated with SVAMITVA.
accepted.tq: Distinguish the complementary digital platforms by their precise functions.
accepted.sec: Capacity building - RGSA, NIRDPR and SIRDs, eGramSwaraj, AuditOnline  [APPSC]

accepted.s:
With reference to eGramSwaraj and SVAMITVA, consider the following statements:
1. eGramSwaraj was launched with SVAMITVA on 24 April 2020.
2. SVAMITVA is associated with the Survey of India.
3. SVAMITVA provides a Record of Rights for rural homes and a baseline for property taxation.
Which of the statements given above are correct?
accepted.x: All three statements are correct. The two initiatives were launched together on 24 April 2020, and SVAMITVA uses the Survey of India framework for rural property records and taxation baselines.
accepted.tq: Combine the launch date, institutional association and substantive purpose in one check.
accepted.sec: Capacity building - RGSA, NIRDPR and SIRDs, eGramSwaraj, AuditOnline  [APPSC]

accepted.s: AuditOnline is primarily intended for:
o: Recommendation of municipal works by Members of Parliament
accepted.x: AuditOnline is the platform for auditing Panchayat accounts online.
accepted.tq: Separate an audit function from planning, property-record and works-recommendation functions.
accepted.sec: Capacity building - RGSA, NIRDPR and SIRDs, eGramSwaraj, AuditOnline  [APPSC]

accepted.s: Training of Trainers under the capacity-building framework has included training on:
accepted.x: Training of Trainers has included the subject of own-source revenue of local bodies.
accepted.tq: Select the local-governance subject that directly relates to Panchayat capacity building.
accepted.sec: Capacity building - RGSA, NIRDPR and SIRDs, eGramSwaraj, AuditOnline  [APPSC]

accepted.s: The recommendation to establish a Local Body Ombudsman was made by the:
o: First Administrative Reforms Commission in its Sixth Report
Second Finance Commission in its Local Finance Report
Second Administrative Reforms Commission in its Sixth Report
accepted.x: The Second Administrative Reforms Commission recommended a Local Body Ombudsman in its Sixth Report, titled Local Governance, published in 2007.
accepted.tq: Discriminate between the First and Second ARC, a standard institutional trap.

accepted.s: The Sixth Report of the Second Administrative Reforms Commission dealing with local governance was published in:
accepted.x: The Second ARC's Sixth Report, titled Local Governance, was published in 2007.
accepted.tq: Test the report number and year together to avoid confusing it with the 2013 expert committee.
accepted.sec: Committees and reports on local devolution - Local Body Ombudsman, 2nd ARC, V. Ramachandran  [other exams]

accepted.s: The V. Ramachandran Expert Committee, constituted by the Ministry of Panchayati Raj in 2013, dealt with:
o: Determining the boundaries of Parliamentary constituencies
Using Panchayats for efficient delivery of public goods and services
accepted.x: The V. Ramachandran Expert Committee examined the use of Panchayats for efficient delivery of public goods and services.
accepted.tq: Match the committee with its stated subject rather than with a general local-government function.
accepted.sec: Committees and reports on local devolution - Local Body Ombudsman, 2nd ARC, V. Ramachandran  [other exams]

accepted.s: Which one of the following is NOT identified as a reason for the underperformance of Panchayati Raj Institutions in the government's Roadmap for Panchayati Raj?
o: Weak devolution of the three Fs
accepted.x: The Roadmap identifies weak 3F devolution, bureaucratic control, tied funds, dependence on grants and reluctance to tax. Complete financial autonomy is not listed and contradicts the identified constraints.
accepted.tq: Find the option that reverses the diagnosed weakness instead of merely naming one.
accepted.sec: Committees and reports on local devolution - Local Body Ombudsman, 2nd ARC, V. Ramachandran  [other exams]

accepted.s: Which State is specifically associated with an Ombudsman for local self-government institutions?
accepted.x: Kerala has an Ombudsman for local self-government institutions.
accepted.tq: Use the State-specific institutional association as the decisive clue.
accepted.sec: Committees and reports on local devolution - Local Body Ombudsman, 2nd ARC, V. Ramachandran  [other exams]

accepted.s:
Match List-I with List-II:

List-I (F)

a. Functions
b. Funds
c. Functionaries

d. Eleventh Schedule

List-II

i. Staff answerable to the local body

ii. Subjects relating to Panchayats

iii. Untied money matching transferred functions

iv. 29 subjects

Select the correct answer using the code given below.
accepted.x: Functions are subjects transferred to local bodies, funds are untied money matching those functions, functionaries are staff answerable to the local body, and the Eleventh Schedule contains 29 Panchayat subjects.
accepted.tq: Start from the sure pair—Functionaries with staff answerable to the local body—and complete the mapping.
accepted.sec: 3Fs devolution - funds, functions, functionaries

accepted.s: Which of the following pairs correctly states the number of subjects in the Eleventh and Twelfth Schedules, respectively?
accepted.x: The Eleventh Schedule contains 29 subjects relating to Panchayats, while the Twelfth Schedule contains 18 subjects relating to municipalities.
accepted.tq: Keep the Panchayat and municipal Schedule counts in their constitutional order.
accepted.sec: 3Fs devolution - funds, functions, functionaries

accepted.s:
Consider the following statements about constitutional devolution to local bodies:
1. The Eleventh and Twelfth Schedules transfer subjects automatically without legislative action.
2. Article 243G relates to Panchayats.
3. Article 243W relates to municipalities.
4. The relevant Articles state that the State legislature may devolve powers and responsibilities.
Which of the statements given above are correct?
accepted.x: Statements 2, 3 and 4 are correct. The Schedules do not themselves transfer subjects automatically; Articles 243G and 243W use the discretionary expression 'may' for devolution.
accepted.tq: Spot the absolute claim that the Schedules themselves transfer functions automatically.
accepted.sec: 3Fs devolution - funds, functions, functionaries

accepted.s: Which one of the following best describes the standard condition of 3F devolution in practice?
o: Staff are answerable to local bodies, while functions and funds are retained by the Union.
Functions, funds and functionaries are fully transferred to local bodies in an untied form.
Funds are untied, but functions remain exclusively with State departments.
Functions are devolved on paper, funds arrive tied to schemes, and staff report to State line departments.
accepted.x: The standard finding is that functions exist on paper, funds are commonly tied to schemes, and functionaries continue to report to State line departments.
accepted.tq: Compare the formal position with the operational reality across all three Fs.
accepted.sec: 3Fs devolution - funds, functions, functionaries

accepted.s: The discretionary character of local devolution is principally linked with which combination of Articles?
accepted.x: Articles 243G and 243W concern devolution of powers and responsibilities, while Articles 243H and 243X concern local taxation and funds; the use of 'may' makes devolution discretionary.
accepted.tq: Group the Articles by their common connection with discretionary devolution and local finances.
accepted.sec: 3Fs devolution - funds, functions, functionaries

accepted.s: The report titled “Status of Devolution to Panchayats in States” is published by the:
o: Ministry of Housing and Urban Affairs, prepared with the National Institute of Urban Affairs
Ministry of Panchayati Raj, prepared with IIPA
Ministry of Rural Development, prepared with NIRDPR
Ministry of Finance, prepared with the Finance Commission
accepted.x: The Devolution Index report is published by the Ministry of Panchayati Raj and is prepared with the Indian Institute of Public Administration.
accepted.tq: Identify the publishing ministry and distinguish it from related rural-development institutions.
accepted.sec: Devolution Index - publisher and AP's rank

accepted.s: Which of the following groups consists entirely of bodies or arrangements identified as bypassing elected local bodies?
o: State Legislatures, Finance Commissions, DPCs and MPCs
DPCs, MPCs, Gram Sabhas and Zila Panchayats
DRDAs, user groups, SHGs and MPLADS/MLA LADS
accepted.x: DRDAs, user groups, SHGs and MPLADS/MLA LADS were identified as arrangements that bypass elected local bodies. DPCs and MPCs are constitutional planning bodies intended to integrate plans.
accepted.tq: Separate parallel or scheme-based bodies from constitutional planning and capacity-building institutions.
accepted.sec: Parallel bodies - DRDAs, user groups, MP/MLA LADS, AP-specific bodies

accepted.s: State-appointed parastatals and Special Purpose Vehicles (SPVs) are criticised in the context of local governance because they:
o: Automatically transfer all functions to Panchayats
Provide untied funds directly to Gram Sabhas
Replace the State Finance Commission constitutionally
Bypass citizen participation and elected local bodies
accepted.x: State-appointed parastatals and SPVs may bypass citizen participation and elected local bodies by operating outside the regular local-government framework.
accepted.tq: Apply the concept of parallel bodies to an institutional scenario.
accepted.sec: Parallel bodies - DRDAs, user groups, MP/MLA LADS, AP-specific bodies

accepted.s: Which of the following correctly matches the Andhra Pradesh-specific arrangements with the period in which they were associated?
o: Janmabhoomi committees—2014-19; village and ward secretariats and volunteers—2019
Janmabhoomi committees—2007-12; village and ward secretariats—2014
Janmabhoomi committees—2019; village and ward secretariats—2014-19
Janmabhoomi committees—2022-26; village and ward secretariats—2018-19
accepted.x: Janmabhoomi committees operated during 2014-19, while village and ward secretariats and volunteers were introduced in 2019; both were criticised as parallel to gram panchayats and wards.
accepted.tq: Match each AP-specific body with its correct period before judging the comparison.
accepted.sec: Parallel bodies - DRDAs, user groups, MP/MLA LADS, AP-specific bodies

accepted.s: The constitutional planning bodies intended to integrate plans at the district and metropolitan levels are, respectively:
o: DPC under Article 243ZD and MPC under Article 243ZE
MPC under Article 243ZD and DPC under Article 243ZE
DPC under Article 243G and MPC under Article 243W
DPC under Article 280 and MPC under Article 281
accepted.x: The District Planning Committee is provided under Article 243ZD, while the Metropolitan Planning Committee is provided under Article 243ZE.
accepted.tq: Match the planning body, territorial level and Article number in sequence.
accepted.sec: Parallel bodies - DRDAs, user groups, MP/MLA LADS, AP-specific bodies

accepted.s: With reference to MPLADS, which one of the following is correct?
o: The Gram Panchayat recommends works and the Election Commission executes them through eSAKSHI.
The Member of Parliament executes the works directly, and RTI does not apply.
The Member of Parliament recommends works, while the Implementing District Authority executes them; RTI applies and the eSAKSHI portal is associated with the scheme.
The State Finance Commission recommends works and the District Planning Committee executes them without any transparency law.
accepted.x: Under MPLADS, the MP recommends works and the Implementing District Authority executes them. RTI applies, and eSAKSHI is the associated portal.
accepted.tq: Ask who recommends and who executes; this separates legislative recommendation from administrative implementation.
accepted.sec: Parallel bodies - DRDAs, user groups, MP/MLA LADS, AP-specific bodies

accepted.s: Which of the following statements about the proposed District Development Council model is correct?
o: It was designed to replace the District Planning Committee under Article 243ZD.
It was criticised as a parallel executive that could bypass Zila Panchayats and Urban Local Bodies.
It was criticised for transferring all executive powers to Gram Sabhas.
It was created to merge MPLADS with the Fifteenth Finance Commission.
accepted.x: The proposed District Development Council model was criticised as a parallel executive arrangement capable of bypassing Zila Panchayats and Urban Local Bodies.
accepted.tq: Identify the institutional criticism rather than infer a constitutional replacement.
accepted.sec: Parallel bodies - DRDAs, user groups, MP/MLA LADS, AP-specific bodies
